Alphabetizing A Table Of Contents In Microsoft Word

Jul 12, 2017 • Janice Cotcher

There are advantages and disadvantages of using either a table of contents or an index in a Word document.  If you insert an index, the contents are automatically are alphabetized, but you cannot create hyperlinks. With a table of contents, each title can be linked to a portion of text but there is no way to automatically alphabetize a table of contents. After an exhaustive online search, I determined the easiest way to gain the benefits of both.

First, you need to generate a table of contents (Here’s a tutorial from Microsoft if you don’t know how).

After the table of contents (TOC) is created, select all of the titles and copy them.

On a new page, paste the contents. Higlight the titles you just pastedand choose “Table” from the “Insert” menu. This creates a table around the text with each title in its own row. Select the contents of the table.

Under the “Home” tab, select “Sort”.

A dialogue box willl appear with your sort options. Sorting by Column 1 in an ascending order will alphabetize the content.

The alphabetized content:

To remove the borders, right click on the table and choose “Borders and Shading”.

Once the dialogue box appears, choose “None” under the “Borders” tab.

Add your title and you have an alphabetized TOC (or index with hyperlinks). You can now delete the TOC generated by Microsoft Word.
